doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Forming the octet and its few gigs
summary: The octet formed in Milhaud's class and played only a handful of concerts; his father called it the damndest noise.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Tell me about the formation of the octet. How did that . . .?
In terms of performing, my understand is that between 1947 and 1949, the octet had only three paying gigs.
But did you also perform – did you get together informally to play and practice?

Yeah. And once in a while, somebody will say, “Oh, but I heard you at University of California, Berkeley.” It’s a gig I forgot. So maybe there were four or five. But there weren’t many. At Mills College, Marines Memorial in San Francisco, College of Pacific in Stockton, University of California, Berkeley.
I’m told that your father, after hearing a concert by the octet, once told a newspaper writer, “That was the damndest bunch of notes I ever heard.” Is that true?
Yeah. He said that, and he meant it. I told him he was the best critic who ever heard me.
